subject.title: [Feature]: Support Anthropic native server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution)

question: Should OpenClaw support Anthropic server-side web_fetch and code_execution/PTC with allowed_callers as a bundled Anthropic plugin/runtime feature, and what opt-in/security boundaries should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but provider-hosted code execution and server-result replay affect product policy, security boundaries, config surface, and session semantics beyond a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Keep Broad Tracker And Design
options.body: Keep this issue open, let narrower web_search work stay separate, and require maintainer-approved product/security design before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Web Search Only
options.body: Close or split the broader code_execution/PTC and web_fetch scope, leaving only the existing Anthropic native web_search tracker.

options.title: Reject Server-Hosted Execution
options.body: Decline Anthropic code_execution/PTC in core for now and document that OpenClaw will keep local/client-side tools or external plugins for this class of capability.

recommendation.title: Keep Broad Tracker And Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, let narrower web_search work stay separate, and require maintainer-approved product/security design before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter posted the prior keep-open review and has recent cross-cutting provider/plugin/config history around the affected boundaries.
